entries.acceptance_scope: independent model-level full-message linguistic and caller-semantic review only
entries.source: This %1$s contains %2$s frames. AN Paint edits still images and does not preserve animation.
entries.candidate: Dette %1$s-biletet har %2$s biletruter. AN Paint redigerer stillbilete og tek ikkje vare på animasjon.
entries.accepted_value: Dette %1$s-biletet har %2$s biletruter. AN Paint redigerer stillbilete og tek ikkje vare på animasjon.
entries.actual_caller_semantics: Preserves format, frame-count string, still-image editing and non-preservation of animation. ImportSelection only selects this counted branch for frameCount >= 2, so plural biletruter is appropriate. Hyphenated %1$s-biletet composes with a format label rather than a numeric or filename argument.
entries.nynorsk_review: Dette, biletet, biletruter, stillbilete and tek ikkje vare på are coherent Nynorsk. The exact-count sentence is idiomatic; the inexact-count sentence necessarily includes the explicitly untouched English qualifier.
entries.composition_review: Exact count example: Dette GIF-biletet har 3 biletruter. AN Paint redigerer stillbilete og tek ikkje vare på animasjon. Inexact count example: Dette GIF-biletet har at least 3 biletruter. AN Paint redigerer stillbilete og tek ikkje vare på animasjon. The latter deliberately retains the English qualifier; %2$s must remain a string. Both are then followed by two newlines and the appropriate poster/still paragraph. This verdict does not establish fully localized composed UI.

entries.source: This image uses a colour profile that AN Paint cannot convert yet. Convert it to sRGB PNG in a colour-managed editor before importing.

entries.actual_caller_semantics: Preserves the unsupported colour-profile condition, current inability to convert it, and the instruction to convert the image to sRGB PNG in an external colour-managed editor before importing. The exceptions originate specifically from UnsupportedColour in DibCodec, IcoCodec and PlatformImageColour, not arbitrary provider failures. No automatic conversion, relabelling or guaranteed future capability is promised.
